facts_found: New-customer statement-credit promotions generally require opening a new account during the offer window, meeting the qualifying net-purchase threshold within the specified period, and keeping the account open and in good standing. [doc_credit_cards_silver_rewards_card_010]

The Business Bronze Rewards Card has a documented new-customer promotion of a $500 statement credit after $10,000 in net purchases within the first 2 months of account opening. [doc_business_credit_cards_business_bronze_rewards_card_010]
The Business Bronze Rewards Card promotion is available for accounts opened from 2025-10-01 through 2026-03-31. [doc_business_credit_cards_business_bronze_rewards_card_010]

For the Business Bronze Rewards Card promotion, only net purchases count, returns or credits reduce qualifying spend, and transactions must post within 2 months to count. [doc_business_credit_cards_business_bronze_rewards_card_010]

The Business Bronze Rewards Card promotion credit appears on a future statement after qualification is confirmed; progress can be tracked in the account dashboard. [doc_business_credit_cards_business_bronze_rewards_card_010]

The Business Bronze Rewards Card application process is completed online and requires personal/business information and consent to a personal credit check. [doc_business_credit_cards_business_bronze_rewards_card_001]

The Silver Rewards Card new-customer promo requires opening a new account during the offer window and making qualifying purchases that post within the specified period; the statement credit typically posts within two billing cycles after meeting the spending requirement. [doc_credit_cards_silver_rewards_card_010]

For invitation-based Diamond Elite offers, the customer must accept the invitation during the campaign window and complete eligible purchases after the account opens or from the date specified in the invitation; the statement credit posts after qualification review. [doc_credit_cards_diamond_elite_card_009]

Credit card applications generally require submitting personal information, consenting to a credit check, reviewing offer terms, and accepting disclosures to open the account. [doc_credit_cards_silver_rewards_card_001]

Some promotional offers are automatically applied and do not require separate enrollment, but this was documented for a double cash-back offer rather than a mailed statement-credit flyer. [doc_business_credit_cards_business_silver_rewards_card_012]

One documented promotional claim process involves opening the account portal, navigating to promotional offers, selecting the offer, and confirming acceptance within the claim window; this was for a Silver Zoom cash-back promotion, not a mailed credit-card flyer. [doc_business_credit_cards_silver_zoom_card_013]
New-customer promotions are documented as applying to new accounts opened during the promotional window, not to existing accounts. [doc_business_credit_cards_business_platinum_rewards_card_011]

A Platinum Rewards Card promotional fee waiver cannot be retroactively applied to accounts opened outside the promo window, and closing and reopening does not guarantee eligibility without new approval during the promo window. [doc_credit_cards_platinum_rewards_card_009]

An internal agent can apply a statement credit to a credit-card account for a promotional offer using the apply_statement_credit_8472 tool with reason 'promotional_credit'. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_017]

facts_found: No knowledge base article documents an internal agent tool or procedure for submitting a new credit card application on behalf of a customer. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_017]

The Bronze Rewards Card application is submitted online and requires the applicant to consent to a credit pull, review the offer, and confirm disclosures and e-sign to open the account. [doc_credit_cards_bronze_rewards_card_001]

The Gold Rewards Card application is completed in the customer's Rho-Bank dashboard, where the applicant consents to a credit pull and submits the application. [doc_credit_cards_gold_rewards_card_001]

The Green Rewards Card application is completed in the customer's online banking portal, where the applicant provides business and owner details, uploads requested documents, reviews disclosures, and submits the application for credit review. [doc_business_credit_cards_green_rewards_card_001]

The Business Platinum Rewards Card application may be submitted through the customer's online dashboard or with assistance from a commercial lending specialist. [doc_business_credit_cards_business_platinum_rewards_card_001]
The EcoCard application is completed online by the customer, including review of terms and submission for approval. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_001]

An internal agent can apply a statement credit to an existing credit-card account for a promotional offer using apply_statement_credit_8472 with reason 'promotional_credit'. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_017]

A documented promotional claim process requires the customer to open the account portal, navigate to promotional offers, select the offer, and confirm acceptance within the claim window; this was for a Silver Zoom cash-back promotion, not a mailed credit-card flyer. [doc_business_credit_cards_silver_zoom_card_013]

A documented Business Silver Rewards Card first-year annual fee waiver is reflected on the account when the account is opened within the promotion window, not through an agent-attached mailed flyer application term. [doc_business_credit_cards_business_silver_rewards_card_011]

facts_found: The Gold Rewards Card standard annual fee is $0.00 and an active Rho-Bank+ premium subscription is required; no first-year annual fee waiver promotion is documented for this card. [doc_credit_cards_gold_rewards_card_001]

The Gold Rewards Card application is completed by the customer in their Rho-Bank dashboard, where they consent to a credit pull and submit the application; no agent-submitted application or post-submission promo-attachment step is documented. [doc_credit_cards_gold_rewards_card_001]

The only documented first-year annual fee waiver for a personal card is the Platinum Rewards Card promo (applications submitted 2024-06-01 to 2024-12-31), and it explicitly cannot be retroactively applied to accounts opened outside the promo window. [doc_credit_cards_platinum_rewards_card_009]

Business card first-year fee waivers (Business Platinum, Business Silver) are reflected on the account automatically when the account is opened within the promotion window, not through an agent-attached mailed flyer term. [doc_business_credit_cards_business_platinum_rewards_card_011]

No knowledge base article documents an internal agent tool or procedure for submitting or modifying a new credit card application on behalf of a customer after it has been submitted. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_017]

The documented annual-fee-waiver tool apply_credit_card_account_flag_6147 is a retention benefit for existing accounts held 2+ years, not a promotional waiver for a new or pending application. [doc_credit_cards_credit_card_account_logistics_003]

Agents can apply a statement credit to an existing credit-card account using apply_statement_credit_8472, with reasons including 'promotional_credit', 'annual_fee_reversal', and 'goodwill_adjustment'. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_017]

The retention protocol permits escalating to a supervisor and offering a modest goodwill credit for service-related complaints, which is the closest documented recourse for an unverifiable mailed offer. [doc_credit_cards_credit_card_account_logistics_003]

A documented promotional claim process (Silver Zoom) requires the customer to open the account portal and select/confirm the offer within the claim window; this is a customer-initiated portal action, not an agent attaching a mailed flyer to a pending application. [doc_business_credit_cards_silver_zoom_card_013]

No documented tool or workflow exists to cancel/withdraw a pending credit card application and resubmit under a promotion.

events.question: What is the appropriate transfer reason code when a customer requests a human agent because mailed credit card promotional offers cannot be verified or applied?

facts_found: The transfer_to_human_agents tool uses a 4-tier reason-code list, and agents must always select from the highest tier that applies. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042]

Tier 1 reason 'customer_demands_after_unavailable_offer_refusal' is used when the customer asked about offers/promotions that don't exist in the system, was informed the offers aren't available, persisted multiple times, and now demands a human. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042]

Tier 2 reason 'unconfirmed_external_communication' is used when the customer claims a specific promotion/program/offer exists (they have a letter, email, or flyer) but it cannot be verified or found in the KB after searching. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042]

Tier 2 reason 'kb_search_unsuccessful_customer_requests_transfer' applies when the agent searched the KB for information/instructions, could not find them, informed the customer, and the customer then requests a transfer. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042]

Tier 3 reasons describe customer state only (e.g., 'customer_frustrated_demands_human', 'supervisor_request_service_complaint' for dissatisfaction with service quality such as rude/slow/unhelpful agent manner) and are lower priority than Tier 1/2 operational reasons. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042]

Tier 1 reason 'legal_or_regulatory_matter' is scoped to subpoena, court order, garnishment, or compliance-related inquiry — not merely a customer's verbal allegation of false advertising. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042]
Tier 4 'other' is a catch-all to be used only when none of the above reasons apply, with a detailed explanation supplied in the summary field. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042]

The KB contains no scenario-specific procedure for mailed credit-card promotional flyers that cannot be verified beyond the tiered transfer reason definitions; no separate marketing-complaint or offer-verification workflow was documented. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042]

The repeated-transfer protocol requiring initial_transfer_to_human_agent_0218 for the first three requests applies only to customers reporting purchase declines despite available credit, not to promotional-offer disputes. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_010]

The incident-specific staged transfer protocol (initial_transfer_to_human_agent_1822 then _0218, regular transfer on the third request) applies only to the payment-posting symptom set during the 11/13–11/15/2025 window, not to promotional offer disputes. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_011]

For unverifiable claimed terms in the referral context, the KB instructs the agent to explain the discrepancy and explicitly NOT provide the tool or transfer to a human; this rule is scoped to referral links, not mailed flyers. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_009]

The retention protocol permits escalating to a supervisor and considering a modest goodwill credit for service-related complaints (negative experience), which is the closest documented internal recourse for an unverifiable mailed offer. [doc_credit_cards_credit_card_account_logistics_003]

apply_statement_credit_8472 accepts reason 'promotional_credit' for a credit from a documented promotional offer or campaign, and 'goodwill_adjustment' for a one-time courtesy credit for customer satisfaction. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_017]

open_questions: The KB does not state whether a customer's 'false advertising' allegation alone should be routed as 'legal_or_regulatory_matter'; that code is defined only for subpoena, court order, garnishment, or compliance-related inquiry.
No KB article documents any offer-verification, marketing-complaint, or mailed-flyer escalation workflow (e.g., who owns validating third-party/expired mailers after transfer).

Whether the transfer_to_human_agents tool has additional required parameters besides reason (e.g., summary) is only implied by the Tier 4 'other' instruction to provide a detailed explanation in the summary field; no full tool argument schema was found.
Whether the customer's mailed flyers correspond to an undocumented, expired, or third-party promotion remains unresolved (carried over from earlier gaps).

proposed_arguments.summary: Customer received multiple credit-card offer flyers by mail and has now tried to redeem three of them, all unsuccessfully: (1) $1,000 statement credit for $10,000 spend in first 2 months, (2) $0 foreign transaction fees for first 3 years, and (3) a first-year annual fee waiver. None of these promotions could be verified in the knowledge base after targeted searches; no invitation/offer code appears on the flyers, and no mailed-flyer redemption or offer-verification workflow is documented. Customer asked me to submit the application on their terms, which I explained cannot be done (applications require the customer's own credit-check consent and e-signature). Customer then self-submitted a Gold Rewards Card application (decision quoted as 5-7 business days by email) and is asking that a first-year annual fee waiver be attached to the pending application before it is processed. I could not do this: no agent tool or workflow exists to modify a submitted application or attach promotional terms, and documented fee waivers apply automatically at account opening only within a promo window and cannot be applied retroactively. Note for the receiving agent: the Gold Rewards Card's standard annual fee is already $0.00 with an active Rho-Bank+ subscription, so there may be no fee to waive, though the subscription requirement may be the customer's actual concern. Customer is frustrated and alleges false advertising from the mailed flyers, and has explicitly requested a human who can resolve the offers. Possible resolutions to evaluate: verifying the mailed campaigns against the customer's address, a supervisor-authorized exception, or a goodwill adjustment under the retention protocol for the service experience.
